title: The Protein Blueprint
philosophicalAnchor: Keratin supports, Amylase catalyzes—both are proteins, both inherit common traits, yet their functions diverge through the magic of inheritance and method overriding.
pythonConcept: object-oriented programming, inheritance, super(), method overriding, polymorphism, class hierarchy
briefDescription: Model protein types in a bio-informatics database using inheritance, demonstrating polymorphism across StructuralProtein and Enzyme subclasses.
theoryPillar: Inheritance creates class hierarchies where subclasses inherit attributes and methods from base classes. super() calls parent constructors and methods. Method overriding redefines inherited behavior in subclasses.
anchorPillar: All proteins have name, sequence, and get_length(). But StructuralProteins provide support while Enzymes catalyze reactions. Both share the Protein interface but implement perform_function() differently.
triggerPillar: The database must catalog different protein types with common traits yet wildly different biological functions. Polymorphism allows treating all proteins uniformly while invoking type-specific behavior.
realityPillar: class Protein: base class with __init__, get_length(), perform_function(). class StructuralProtein(Protein): inherits and overrides perform_function(). class Enzyme(Protein): adds target_molecule and overrides perform_function().
